messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: Elevated 5xx/timeouts observed from private deployments in us-west-2. 12% 5xx rate on inference-gateway-proxy, spike started ~10m ago. Auto-escalation to oncall
maria_oncall: I'm on it. Can you paste the alert detail and affected resource IDs? :phone:
incident-bot: Alert details: metric=5xx_rate, service=inference-gateway-proxy, env=private-usw2, window=5m, value=0.12, threshold=0.03\nTop traces show TCP timeouts to 13.32.100.0/22 (egress NAT pool) and frequent RSTs. Affected customers: 3 private tenants (tenant-a, tenant-b, tenant-c).
kevin_sre: grabbing k8s logs from gateway pods now. docker image: redwood/gateway:stable-2026-02. Running `kubectl -n infra logs deployment/inference-gateway -c proxy --tail=200`
oliver_runtime: I see repeated outbound ECONNRESET when connecting to model-store.s3.amazonaws.com from the gateway. Likely egress path problem or conntrack exhaustion. How are these private deployments egressing? NAT instances or managed NAT GW?
sanjay_netops: These private clusters use NAT instances with ip-masquerade on t3.mediums in each AZ. We also have a transit route to a partner appliance but that's fallthrough only.
carol_support: Customer-impact note: tenant-b reported increased request latency and 502s on their test traffic at 13:38 UTC. They escalated to SEs.
maria_oncall: OK; plan: (1) verify conntrack on NAT instance (2) check iptables MASQUERADE rules (3) test egress curl from a gateway pod to 8.8.8.8 and to s3 endpoint (4) if NAT instance unhealthy, failover to spare NAT or change route table to use transit appliance.
kevin_sre: Running on NAT instance (10.0.12.45): `sudo conntrack -S` shows conntrack entries maxed, counters: found=65536, hash-entries=65536. `cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max` -> 65536. That explains resets.
kevin_sre: Also `sudo iptables -t nat -L -n -v` shows no MASQUERADE rule in POSTROUTING for eth0. Looks like iptables rules flushed - maybe a kernel update/restart of the network agent.
oliver_runtime: If MASQUERADE gone, return traffic won't be NATed and will get dropped. That matches the TCP RST/timeouts.
sanjay_netops: Can we bump nf_conntrack_max temporarily? `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=200000` and re-add MASQUERADE rule: `iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -o eth0 -j MASQUERADE`
maria_oncall: Do it in canary AZ first (us-west-2a) and measure.
kevin_sre: Applying on NAT instance 10.0.12.45 now:\n```
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=200000
sudo iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -o eth0 -j MASQUERADE
```
kevin_sre: After change: conntrack_max=200000, conntrack count dropped slightly as old entries aged. Re-added MASQUERADE rule present.
kevin_sre: Running simple curl from gateway pod (k8s pod gateway-67c): `kubectl -n infra exec -it gateway-67c -- curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{time_total}\n' https://model-store.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/ping` -> previously timed out, now 200 0.24s :white_check_mark:
oliver_runtime: Rolling changes to other AZs now. Will patch NAT instances in us-west-2b and 2c with same sysctl+iptables fix. Also patch drift detection to alert if MASQUERADE missing.
sanjay_netops: Side note: looking at cloud-init logs, there was a package update at 01:30 UTC that restarted conntrack service and cleared iptables-save restore failed on that host. Need a durable iptables restore on boot.
carol_support: Noting mitigation: applied conntrack increase and restored MASQUERADE rules; customer-facing status: degraded -> partial outage for affected private tenants from 13:30-13:55 UTC. I'll notify tenant contacts and provide RCA pending.
maria_oncall: After AZ patches, 5xx rate dropped from 12% -> 1.2% in 7m. Monitoring shows stable. Still keep on-call rotation until 14:10 UTC and run post-incident checklist.
deploy-bot: Deploy window recorded: rollback not performed. Change set: manual iptables/sysctl on NAT instances (out-of-band) by kevin_sre maria_oncall.
kevin_sre: Next steps: create a boot-time iptables restore unit, add conntrack_max increase to instance launch config, and create alert when MASQUERADE missing (detect via `iptables -t nat -C POSTROUTING -o eth0 -j MASQUERADE` exit code).
oliver_runtime: I'll add a runtime guard in gateway to fallback to a routed egress (transit appliance) if outbound socket errors exceed threshold for 3m. That gives graceful degradation.
sanjay_netops: I'll open a ticket to migrate NAT instances to managed NAT Gateway in high-traffic private clusters, and add automation for conntrack tuning.
maria_oncall: Thanks everyone. I'll take incident to postmortem channel and draft customer RCA. Marking thread resolved once we confirm 30m stable.
carol_support: Quick note for RCA draft: timeline, mitigation commands, affected tenants, mitigation message sent. I'll attach logs and k8s snapshots.
kevin_sre: Uploading conntrack and iptables captures to /mnt/incidents/1968453210/ (links: s3://redwood-incidents/1968453210/conntrack.txt)
incident-bot: Incident status changed: mitigated -> monitoring. If 5xx_rate < 0.02 for 30m, auto-close.
maria_oncall: Monitoring green at 14:02 UTC. Leaving note: root cause = NAT instance iptables restore failure + low conntrack_max; contributing = automated package update that restarted network stack. Postmortem in #postmortems will follow. :white_check_mark:
carol_support: Customer follow-up message prepared and sent to tenant-b with mitigation summary and ETA for permanent fix.
kevin_sre: I'll prepare the infra CL to increase conntrack on AMI and add iptables-restore unit. Assigning to sanjay_netops for implementation.\n
maria_oncall: closing thread here, moving to #postmortems for RCA and action items. Great work team. :clap:
